title: Corneal Dystrophies, Keratoconus and Miscellaneous Disorders

questions.q: Corneal dystrophies are ___ corneal diseases.
questions.exp: Features of corneal dystrophies: primary corneal disease. (Book p180)

questions.q: In which decades of life do corneal dystrophies present?
questions.exp: Corneal dystrophies: present in 1st and 2nd decades. (Book p180)

questions.q: True or false — 'Corneal dystrophies are inflammatory, non-progressive and usually unilateral.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - they are inflammatory and unilateral
False - they are non-inflammatory, progressive and bilateral (B/L)
False - they are inflammatory, progressive and bilateral
False - they are non-inflammatory, non-progressive and unilateral
questions.exp: Features: non-inflammatory, progressive, B/L. (Book p180)

questions.q: Which inheritance pattern is given as the general feature of corneal dystrophies?
questions.exp: Features: autosomal dominant inheritance (exceptions in the table include AR macular dystrophy and AR CHED). (Book p180)

questions.q: Which epithelial dystrophy, also called map dot, is the most common corneal dystrophy?
questions.exp: 1. Epithelial: Cogan's epithelial basement membrane dystrophy/map dot: m/c corneal dystrophy. (Book p180)

questions.q: An epithelial dystrophy is non-progressive and is due to a keratin gene mutation. Which dystrophy is this?
questions.exp: Meesmann epithelial dystrophy: non-progressive, d/t keratin gene mutation. (Book p180)

questions.q: The inheritance listed for Lisch epithelial dystrophy is ___.
questions.exp: Lisch epithelial dystrophy: AD/XLD. (Book p180)

questions.q: Reis Buckler's, Schnyder central crystalline and Thiel Behnke dystrophies are grouped in the table under which layer?
questions.exp: Row group 2. Bowman layer lists Reis Buckler's, Schnyder central crystalline and Thiel Behnke dystrophies. (Book p180)

questions.q: Match the Bowman layer dystrophy with its feature — 1) Reis Buckler's  2) Schnyder central crystalline  3) Thiel Behnke  … A) Honeycomb pattern of opacities  B) Fish net  C) Corneal lipid metabolism disorder
questions.exp: Reis Buckler's: fish net; Schnyder central crystalline: corneal lipid metabolism disorder; Thiel Behnke: honeycomb pattern of opacities. (Book p180)

questions.q: As printed in the table, both Reis Buckler's dystrophy (with CDB1) and Thiel Behnke dystrophy carry which label?
questions.exp: Reis Buckler's dystrophy/CDB1/GCD III and Thiel Behnke dystrophy / GCD III. (Book p180)

questions.q: In lattice corneal dystrophy I (Biber Haab Dimmer) and II (Finnish), neuropathy is seen at what age?
questions.exp: 3. Stromal: Lattice corneal dystrophy I/Biber Haab Dimmer and II/Finnish: neuropathy seen 70-90 years. (Book p180)

questions.q: A lattice dystrophy is AR and has a mulberry-like appearance. Which type is this?
questions.exp: Lattice corneal dystrophy IIIA: AR, mulberry-like appearance. (Book p180)

questions.q: The lattice dystrophies show which deposit and stain in the table?
opts: Hyaline deposit stained by Masson trichome
Acid mucopolysaccharide deposit stained by Alcian blue
Amyloid deposit stained by Congo red
questions.exp: Lattice dystrophies (merged cell): Amyloid deposit: stained by Congo red. (Book p180)

questions.q: Which stromal dystrophy (Japanese) shows a hyaline deposit stained by Masson trichome stain?
questions.exp: Gelatinous drop like dystrophy/Japanese: Hyaline deposit: stained by Masson Trichome stain. (Book p180)

questions.q: Granular corneal dystrophy I (Groenaw granular dystrophy II) shows which deposit?
questions.exp: Granular corneal dystrophy I/Groenaw granular corneal dystrophy II: Hyaline + Amyloid deposit. (Book p180)

questions.q: Macular dystrophy (Groenow II) is AR and the ___ common corneal dystrophy (L/C).
questions.exp: Macular dystrophy/Groenow II: AR, L/C corneal dystrophy. (Book p180)

questions.q: Francois central cloudy dystrophy is an inborn error of the metabolism of:
questions.exp: Francois central cloudy dystrophy: inborn error of keratin sulphate metabolism. (Book p180)

questions.q: Which endothelial dystrophy shows corneal guttata, described as wart-like excrescences?
questions.exp: 4. Endothelial: Fuch's endothelial dystrophy: corneal guttata: wart-like excrescences. (Book p180)

questions.q: Which endothelial dystrophy has a dash (no feature written) in the table's Feature column?
questions.exp: Posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy: '-' in the Feature column. (Book p180)

questions.q: Congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy I and II both have which inheritance and onset?
opts: AR inheritance and onset in the 2nd decade
AD/XLD inheritance and onset in old age
questions.exp: CHED I and II: both have AR inheritance and have perinatal onset. (Book p180)

questions.q: A clinical photograph shows microcysts in the corneal epithelium. Which dystrophy is captioned?
questions.exp: Figure: Meesmann epithelial dystrophy - microcysts in corneal epithelium. (Book p181)

questions.q: In macular dystrophy, the Alcian blue stain shows deposits of:
questions.exp: Macular dystrophy figure: Acid mucopolysaccharidosis deposits; Alcian blue stain. (Book p181)

questions.q: Match the stain in lattice dystrophy type 1 with its finding — 1) PAS stain  2) Congo red stain  … A) Apple green birefringence  B) Amorphous deposit  C) Hyaline deposits
questions.exp: Lattice corneal dystrophy type 1: PAS stain - amorphous deposit; Congo red stain - apple green birefringence. (Book p181)

questions.q: In granular dystrophy, the Masson trichome stain shows:
questions.exp: Granular dystrophy: Masson trichome stain - hyaline deposits. (Book p181)

questions.q: A slit lamp photograph shows bread crumb like granules separated by well-demarcated clear space. Which dystrophy does the book show?
questions.exp: Granular dystrophy figure: bread crumb like granules; label: separated by well-demarcated clear space. (Book p181)

questions.q: Fuch's endothelial dystrophy is written in the book as due to mutation of which gene?
opts: The COAXa gene (as handwritten in the book)
questions.exp: Fuch's endothelial dystrophy: mutation of COAXa gene (as handwritten). (Book p181)

questions.q: Which structures are damaged in Fuch's endothelial dystrophy, producing wart-like excrescences on the cornea?
questions.exp: Fuch's: Descemet membrane + Endothelium damaged; wart-like excrescences on cornea. (Book p181)

questions.q: Which finding in the histology figure of Fuch's dystrophy is labelled 'Diagnostic'?
questions.exp: Figure caption: Corneal guttae (Diagnostic). (Book p181)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a cause of recurrent corneal erosions?
questions.exp: Recurrent corneal erosions - causes: Cogan dystrophy, Thiel Behnke dystrophy, Reis Buckler dystrophy, Lattice type I. (Book p181)

questions.q: Among the lattice dystrophies, recurrent corneal erosions are listed for lattice type ___.
questions.exp: Recurrent corneal erosions - 4. Lattice type I. (Book p181)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the listed metabolic causes of dystrophy?
questions.exp: Metabolic causes of dystrophy: 1. Meesmann epithelial dystrophy, 2. Macular dystrophy, 3. Schnyder central crystalline dystrophy. (Book p182)

questions.q: What is the treatment of corneal dystrophy when visual loss is present?
questions.exp: Treatment of corneal dystrophies: if visual loss +: keratoplasty/corneal transplantation. (Book p182)

questions.q: Keratoconus is a form of corneal ___ and is non-inflammatory, progressive and usually B/L.
questions.exp: Keratoconus: form of corneal ectasia; non-inflammatory, progressive, usually B/L. (Book p182)

questions.q: The first cause listed for keratoconus etiology is:
questions.exp: Etiology: 1. Congenital weakness; 2. Associated with trauma, vernal keratoconjunctivitis, Down syndrome. (Book p182)

questions.q: Keratoconus is associated with all of the following in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Associated with: trauma, vernal keratoconjunctivitis, Down syndrome. (Book p182)

questions.q: The refractive error listed first in the clinical features of keratoconus is ___.
questions.exp: Clinical features: 1. Myopic astigmatism. (Book p182)

questions.q: Examination of keratoconus reveals the hallmark sign. Where is the stromal thinning located?
opts: Central only, with a clear zone at the periphery
questions.exp: 2. Hallmark: Stromal thinning (Central/paracentral) -> Inferior to the centre. (Book p182)

questions.q: Match the keratoconus sign with its description — 1) Munson's sign  2) Rizzuti's sign  … A) Arrowhead pattern of light over the nasal limbus (light from the temporal side)  B) Bulging of lower eyelid on downgaze  C) Stromal stress lines
questions.exp: Munson's sign: bulging of lower eyelid on downgaze. Rizzuti's sign: light from temporal side -> arrowhead pattern of light over nasal limbus. (Book p182)

questions.q: Match the examination technique with the reflex in keratoconus — 1) Retinoscopy  2) Ophthalmoscopy  … A) Oil droplet reflex  B) Scissoring reflex  C) Fleischer ring
questions.exp: 5. On retinoscopy: scissoring reflex. 6. On ophthalmoscopy: oil droplet reflex. (Book p182)

questions.q: Vogt's striae in keratoconus are:
opts: Clear zone between arcus and limbus
Deposits of calcium in Bowman's layer
questions.exp: 7. Vogt's striae: Stromal stress lines. (Book p182)

questions.q: The three keratoconus photographs at the bottom of p182 are captioned:
opts: Munson's sign, Rizzuti's sign and Oil droplet reflex
Rizzuti's sign, Munson's sign and Oil droplet reflex
Munson's sign, Oil droplet reflex and Rizzuti's sign
Vogt's striae, Rizzuti's sign and Oil droplet reflex
questions.exp: Captions: Munson's sign, Rizzuti's sign, Oil droplet reflex. (Book p182)

questions.q: What is the investigation of choice (IOC) for diagnosing keratoconus?
questions.exp: Diagnosis: IOC: Corneal topography. (Book p182)

questions.q: What is the risk noted with a rigid contact lens for keratoconus?
opts: It causes calcium deposits in Bowman's layer
questions.exp: Treatment: Rigid contact lens (may lead to opacity). (Book p183)

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as treatment of keratoconus?
questions.exp: Keratoconus treatment: rigid contact lens, keratoplasty, C3R. Chelation with EDTA is for band shaped keratopathy. (Book p183)

questions.q: C3R is corneal collagen cross linking using ___.
questions.exp: C3R (corneal collagen cross linking using riboflavin and UVA radiation). (Book p183)

questions.q: Band shaped keratopathy is due to deposits of ___ in Bowman's layer.
questions.exp: Band shaped keratopathy: d/t deposits of calcium in Bowman's layer. (Book p183)

questions.q: What is the treatment of band shaped keratopathy?
questions.exp: Band shaped keratopathy - Treatment: Chelation with EDTA. (Book p183)

questions.q: Arcus senilis occurs in old age due to lipid deposition on which structure?
questions.exp: Arcus senilis: occurs in old age; d/t lipid deposition on Descemet's membrane near periphery. (Book p183)

questions.q: The lucid interval of Vogt is the:
opts: Band of calcium in Bowman's layer
Clear zone of cornea between the arcus and the limbus
questions.exp: Lucid interval of Vogt: clear zone of cornea b/w arcus and limbus (Arcus senilis figure). (Book p183)

questions.q: Interstitial keratitis is inflammation only of the corneal ___.
questions.exp: Interstitial keratitis: inflammation only of corneal stroma. (Book p183)

questions.q: Which is NOT a listed cause of interstitial keratitis?
questions.exp: Interstitial keratitis causes: congenital syphilis, Cogan syndrome, tuberculosis, HSV. (Book p183)

questions.q: A patient has interstitial keratitis together with deafness. Which syndrome does the book name?
questions.exp: Cogan syndrome (interstitial keratitis + deafness). (Book p183)

questions.q: Keratoplasty is also known as ___.
questions.exp: Keratoplasty: AKA corneal transplantation. (Book p183)

questions.q: Match the keratoplasty type with the thickness — 1) Penetrating keratoplasty  2) Lamellar keratoplasty  … A) Partial thickness  B) Full thickness  C) Endothelium only
questions.exp: Types: 1. Penetrating keratoplasty (Full thickness); 2. Lamellar keratoplasty (Partial thickness). (Book p183)

questions.q: Expand the two lamellar keratoplasty types — 1) DSEK  2) DALK  … A) Deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty  B) Descemet's stripping endothelial keratoplasty  C) Deep stromal endothelial keratoplasty
questions.exp: DSEK (Descemet's stripping endothelial keratoplasty); DALK (Deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty). (Book p183)

questions.q: Penetrating keratoplasty removes the epithelium to the endothelium, i.e. how many layers?
questions.exp: Removal of - Penetrating keratoplasty: epithelium to endothelium (i.e. all 5 layers). (Book p184)

questions.q: Only the endothelium and Descemet's membrane are removed in a lamellar procedure. Which procedure is this?
questions.exp: DSEK: only endothelium & Descemet's membrane (i.e. posterior 2 layers). (Book p184)

questions.q: DALK removes corneal tissue from the epithelium up to the stroma, i.e. which layers?
questions.exp: DALK: corneal tissue from epithelium upto stroma (i.e. anterior 3 layers). (Book p184)

questions.q: Match the keratoplasty with the indication in the table — 1) Penetrating keratoplasty  2) DSEK  3) DALK  … A) Acute hydrops in severe keratoconus  B) Pseudophakic bullous keratopathy  C) No indication written (dash)
questions.exp: Indication: penetrating keratoplasty - pseudophakic bullous keratopathy; DSEK - dash; DALK - acute hydrops in severe keratoconus. (Book p184)

questions.q: What does the unlabelled last row of the keratoplasty table contain?
opts: Cross-section diagrams of the cornea for the three procedures
Graft survival rates for the three procedures
Storage media for the three procedures
questions.exp: The table's last row shows curved corneal cross-section diagrams under Penetrating keratoplasty, DSEK and DALK. (Book p184)

questions.q: In the procedure, the host cornea is cut using a ___ of diameter 7.5 mm.
questions.exp: Procedure: Host cornea cut using a trephine (Diameter: 7.5 mm) -> implant the graft cornea. (Book p184)

questions.q: The graft cornea is how much larger in diameter than the host opening?
questions.exp: Implant the graft cornea (Diameter: 0.25 mm larger than host opening). (Book p184)

questions.q: The photographs on p184 beside the procedure are captioned:
questions.exp: Figure captions: Trephine; Post-keratoplasty. (Book p184)

questions.q: After keratoplasty, which is the most common type of graft rejection and which line is diagnostic?
opts: Stromal rejection; lucid interval of Vogt
questions.exp: Graft rejection: endothelial rejection (m/c) - forms Khodadoust line (diagnostic). (Book p184)

questions.q: Short-term storage of donor cornea is for < 48 hrs under which conditions?
opts: Room temperature in McCarey Kaufman medium
questions.exp: Short term: < 48 hrs; 4°C, moist chamber/McCarey Kaufman medium. (Book p184)

questions.q: What is the duration of intermediate-term corneal storage?
questions.exp: Intermediate term: < 2 weeks (no other feature written). (Book p184)

questions.q: A donor cornea is cryopreserved at -70°C. Which storage category and duration does the book give?
questions.exp: Long term: up to 35 days; cryopreservation (-70°C). (Book p184)
